source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Thoroughly review stationery sources for any irregularities in emissions monitoring equipment.
3. Check continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) data for anomalies.
4. Record the time and date of each emissions spike or exceedance.
5. Identify the regulated pollutants present in the emissions (e.g., CO2, SO2, NOx, PM).
6. Include background data on usual emissions levels and compare them to the observed excessive levels.
7. Take note of meteorological conditions that may be influencing or impacting emission dispersion.
8. Record any maintenance or operational activities that could correlate with the observed exceedances.
9. Collect and report operational data such as fuel consumption, production rates, and technical specifications.
10. Use standard methods to calculate excessive emissions (e.g., use emission factors, mass balance, or other EPA-approved methods).
11. Compare emissions data with permit limits and applicable regulatory standards.
